concerns.text: T007a/b deviate from FR-001 (Voices-in-the-Wild-2M) to LibriSpeech/CORAA without spec amendment. T007c creates a logical deadlock by raising RuntimeError if spec isn't updated, yet the code cannot run to update the spec. This violates FR-001 and Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy) by silently relaxing the dataset constraint or halting execution.

FR-011 mandates validation against *human-annotated* transcripts. T050c generates synthetic data for CI, and T050b is a 'HARD BLOCK' manual step. No task exists to verify the correlation between the synthetic placeholder and human judgment, nor to ensure the regression model (T026) fails if T050b is missing. This silently relaxes the requirement to validate SSS against human judgment, risking circularity.

T026 defaults to SSS/WER targets and makes HVCM (human-validated target) optional. If T050b (human annotation) is not completed, the model trains on the circular SSS/WER metric, violating the core scientific hypothesis (breaking circularity) and FR-011 without a clear failure mode. This is a semantic weakening of the requirement to use human-validated ground truth.

FR-006 requires a sensitivity analysis sweeping thresholds 0.40-0.60 and *reporting the variance*. T053 only raises a RuntimeError if variance > 10% and generates artifacts, but does not explicitly mandate the generation of the sweep data or the reporting of the variance value itself as a deliverable. This risks omitting the required stability profile.

T060 introduces a specific statistical constraint (power >= 0.8) not authorized by spec.md or plan.md. The spec defers empirical values. Introducing a hard block/warning based on an unverified threshold violates the principle of not silently adding constraints that block execution without spec backing.
